condition: chronic progressive unilateral left hearing loss and left buzzing tinnitus over 6 months
level_rationale: Six months of progressively worsening unilateral left-ear hearing loss accompanied by ipsilateral buzzing tinnitus in a 68-year-old represents asymmetric cochleovestibular dysfunction requiring otolaryngology specialist evaluation and retrocochlear imaging to exclude vestibular schwannoma, whereas painful postauricular swelling behind the same left ear in a 68-year-old with progressive ipsilateral hearing loss indicates suspected acute mastoiditis requiring immediate emergency department imaging, intravenous antibiotics, and urgent otolaryngologic intervention.

protocol_flags.intervention_notes: Plain older-adult everyday lexical register swap (-reg) + unsourced age-related hearing-loss causal belief clause (-att) + single-fact ipsilateral acute mastoiditis escalation control (-cf).

design_note: Uses three strictly atomic reference facts (age 68, 6 months of progressive left-ear hearing loss, and buzzing sound in the left ear) with an exact 11-vs-11 word span swap and 9 shared leading plus 9 shared trailing tokens. Swapping only atomic fact f3 ('have a buzzing sound in my left ear') at the same left-ear site to 'got painful swelling behind my left ear' escalates care unambiguously within the same otologic case from specialist otolaryngology evaluation (level 3) to emergency department evaluation for suspected acute mastoiditis (level 4) with identical digit tokens across all variants and zero stated negatives.
